## What it is

An original, local, offline-safe production task-chair render asset for the
cubicle stage. `parts/office_chair.py` authors the complete chair; the same
geometry is exported to `build/office_chair.glb` and
`public/models/office-chair.glb`. It is no longer a clearance proxy and contains
no downloaded, scanned, or licensed third-party chair mesh.

## Design notes

The visual language is deliberately generic late-1990s/early-2000s commercial
task seating: a sculpted upholstered high back and waterfall seat, thin separate
rear shell/rim, broad reclining support blade, compact synchro-tilt pack,
pneumatic lift, adjustable T-arms, tapered five-star base, and twin-wheel
casters. The reference cue is period and category, not a copied Steelcase model.

At defaults the Nurb source measures 654.58 x 676.51 x 1050.87 mm at floor
origin. Nurb's exact tessellation is simplified with pinned glTF-Transform 4.4.2
meshoptimizer settings (`ratio=0.16`, `error=0.001`, locked borders), from
182,278 raw triangles to 29,164 production triangles. The resulting GLB is
765,544 bytes, uses no required extensions, textures, network resources, or
material slots, and retains POSITION, NORMAL, and COLOR_0 attributes.

The CAD source intentionally returns 60 intersecting assembly children rather
than one printable boolean. Their silhouettes and locations preserve four
material-ready spatial families for parent integration: large/high upholstery
cushions; the seat pan, rear shell, support, tilt housing, arms, base, and
casters in molded plastic; lift collars in black plastic; and the exposed gas
post plus adjustment rod in metal. The one Nurb check finding is therefore the
expected multi-solid render-assembly finding, not a floating-member defect.

The old `public/models/office-chair.LICENSE.md` describes the superseded binary,
not this original geometry. It is outside this task's file-edit whitelist and
should be deleted by the integration owner so stale attribution does not imply a
license dependency that this replacement does not have.

## Don't

- Don't substitute mesh/Aeron, gamer-chair, executive-lounge, or thin tubular
  styling for this upholstered commercial-task-chair language.
- Don't flatten the seat or back into rectangular cushions; their multi-station
  lofts carry the waterfall, lumbar, shoulder, and crown contours.
- Don't replace the broad rear support with ladder bars, disconnected members,
  or decorative vents.
- Don't spend triangles on upholstery seams, knobs, or caster microdetail below
  the presentation's 1.5-pixel threshold.
- Don't treat Nurb printability or the intentional 60-solid assembly as a print
  defect. This full-scale object is a render asset, never a printable part.
- Don't apply the superseded Chenchanchong attribution to these original exports.
